summary: Sweta Prajapati is an Indologist who earned her Ph.D. from Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (1994–1997). She was a Director there (2014), Director in-Charge at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 2015), and Director at the University of Chicago (attested 2015–2016).

Sybrandus Johannes Warren (1847–1910) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his Ph.D. at Leiden University under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern and served as Director of Johan de Witt-gymnasium (1879–1896) and Erasmiaans Gymnasium (1896–1910).

Sydney Frank Markham (1897–1975) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Wadham College (~1920–1923) and served as Secretary and later President of the Museums Association (~1929–1942).
Syed Akbar Hyder is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He has held academic posts at Harvard University (attested 1995) and the University of Texas at Austin.

Syed Ali Bilgrami (1853–1911) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Patna College, Lucknow, Roorkee, Royal School of Mines, and London. He served the Government of Hyderabad (~1881–1901) and became Reader in Marathi at Cambridge in 1901.

Syed Ameer Ali (1849–1928) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at Aliah University and the University of Calcutta (~1867–1868), later holding a post at the University of Calcutta (~1873–1878).

Syed Hasan Askari (1901–1990) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Zila School Chapra, Langat Singh College, and Patna University (MA ~1922–1924), he succeeded Anant Sadashiv Altekar as Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1968–1971).
Syed Nawab Ali was a scholar of history and archaeology. Attested in 1932, he served as Principal of Bahauddin College and Professor of Persian at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda.

Sylvain Brocquet is a French Indologist and linguist who studied at École Normale Supérieure and under Marie-Claude Porcher. He became a Professor at Aix-Marseille University (attested 2023) and President of the Association française pour les études indiennes (attested 2024).

Sylvain Lévi (1863–1935) was a French Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Sorbonne under Abel Bergaigne. He held chairs at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1885–1935) and the Collège de France (1890–1935).

Sylvie Hureau is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies. She has held posts as maître de conférences at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2012) and Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Sze-bong Tso is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed his PhD at the Australian National University (1977–1982) under the supervision of Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana.

Sámuel Brassai (1800–1897) worked in linguistics, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at János Zsigmond Unitarian Highschool, he held professorships at the John Sigismund Unitarian Academy (1837), Ludovika Military Academy (1848), and Franz Joseph University (1872–1884).

Sándor Kégl (1862–1920) was an Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies scholar. He earned his Ph.D. at Eötvös Loránd University under Ignác Goldziher and Ármin Vámbéry, becoming Privatdozent of Persian there in 1893.

Sándor Kőrösi Csoma (1784–1842) was a Hungarian scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Bethlen Gábor College, Göttingen, and under Tibetan teachers including Sangye Phuntsok. He later served as Librarian for The Asiatic Society (1831, 1837–1841).
Søren Ludvig Tuxen (1850–1919) was an educator who completed his early studies at Østre Borgerdyd school by 1868 and subsequently held a post there beginning in 1875.

Søren Sørensen (1848–1902) was a Danish Indologist and linguist. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Copenhagen, studying under Madvig and Westergaard, taught at Herlufsholm School, and became a Docent at Copenhagen in 1899.
Sāmaṇera Bodhesako (1939–1988) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. During his career, he served as an editor for the Buddhist Publication Society and founded Path Press.
Sīlaratano is a Buddhist figure who undertook studies under Narada Maha Thera, Nyanaponika Thera, and Ajahn Maha Bua (~1977–2011).

T. Chandrasekharan is an Indologist who studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He succeeded T. R. Chintamani and served as Professor of History of Sanskrit Language and Literature at Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1951).
